# Chart reference

Every chart's metadata and its `values.yaml` with the comments that document each value.

## capi-cluster-class

The ClusterClass of one cluster and its five templates for CAPN's unprivileged
kubeadm path: LXCClusterTemplate, KubeadmControlPlaneTemplate, KubeadmConfigTemplate
and the control-plane and worker LXCMachineTemplates.

Version `2.0.0`, appVersion `0.9.1`. `values.schema.json` validates the values (`additionalProperties: false`).

```yaml
# capi-cluster-class — the ClusterClass of one cluster.
#
# The ClusterClass is named after the cluster. Each template is named
# <cluster>-<kind>-<8 hex of the sha256 of its spec>: changing a value that
# reaches a template gives that template a new name, the ClusterClass points at
# it, Cluster API rolls the affected machines, and Helm removes the old
# template. What the unprivileged LXC substrate requires (container instances,
# the capi-* profiles, the kubelet flags, dual-stack node addresses) is in the
# templates and cannot be switched off here.

# The cluster this class serves (required); also the ClusterClass name.
cluster:
  name: ""

# The CAPN identity Secret in the release namespace (required).
capn:
  infrastructureSecretName: ""

# The external IPv6 network the nodes' eth1 is on (required): NodePorts answer
# only there. Its router's advertisements give eth1 its address and routes.
externalNetwork:
  ipv6Prefix: ""

controlPlane:
  # CAPN replaces VERSION with the machine's Kubernetes version.
  image:
    ref: "capi:kubeadm/VERSION"
    fingerprint: ""
  # LXD instance flavor (CPU and memory preset); empty = LXD's default.
  flavor: ""
  # LXD profiles after capi-base and capi-controlplane, and device overrides
  # ("<name>,<key>=<value>,...").
  profilesExtra: []
  devicesExtra: []
  # kubeadm ClusterConfiguration and kubelet extras: lists of {name, value}.
  # Reserved (the schema rejects them): bind-address and service-cluster-ip-range
  # (API server); allocate-node-cidrs, cluster-cidr and service-cluster-ip-range
  # (controller manager); feature-gates, node-ip and provider-id (kubelet).
  featureGates: {}
  apiServerExtraArgs: []
  controllerManagerExtraArgs: []
  schedulerExtraArgs: []
  kubeletExtraArgs: []
  preKubeadmCommands: []
  postKubeadmCommands: []
  # Lifetime of the certificates kubeadm issues on control-plane nodes (Cluster
  # API allows 1-1095), and how many days before they expire Cluster API rolls
  # the control-plane machines (at least 7, smaller than the lifetime).
  certificateValidityPeriodDays: 1095
  certificatesExpiryDays: 60

worker:
  image:
    ref: "capi:kubeadm/VERSION"
    fingerprint: ""
  flavor: ""
  # After capi-base and capi-worker.
  profilesExtra: []
  devicesExtra: []
  # Reserved: feature-gates, node-ip, provider-id.
  kubeletExtraArgs: []
  preKubeadmCommands: []
  postKubeadmCommands: []

# The HAProxy load-balancer instance CAPN creates in front of the control plane.
loadBalancer:
  # {name, server, protocol, fingerprint}; empty = CAPN's haproxy image.
  image: {}
  flavor: ""
  # Member or @group of an LXD cluster; empty on a single host.
  target: ""
  disableHealthzCheck: false
  # After capi-base.
  profilesExtra: []
```

## capi-workload-cluster

One Cluster API Cluster in topology mode, on the ClusterClass of the same name
(charts/capi-cluster-class), and the hook that publishes its API server on the
LXD host.

Version `2.0.0`, appVersion `1.14.4`. `values.schema.json` validates the values (`additionalProperties: false`).

```yaml
# capi-workload-cluster — one Cluster in topology mode.
#
# The Cluster uses the ClusterClass of the same name in the release namespace
# (charts/capi-cluster-class with the same cluster.name). After every install
# and upgrade a hook Job publishes the API server through an LXD proxy device on
# the load-balancer instance and waits until it answers; the port is in the
# Cluster's `k8s-lab.io/api-proxy-port` annotation.

cluster:
  # Required: the Cluster and its ClusterClass (charts/capi-cluster-class).
  name: ""
  # Revision of the ClusterClass release, recorded in the Cluster's
  # `k8s-lab.io/class-revision` annotation; 0 = none.
  classRevision: 0

# topology.version. It needs a `capi:kubeadm/<version>` image on CAPN's image
# server (https://images.linuxcontainers.org/capn/streams/v1/images.json).
kubernetes:
  version: "v1.37.0"

topology:
  # Odd (stacked etcd).
  controlPlane:
    replicas: 3
  workers:
    replicas: 2

# [IPv4, IPv6] each.
clusterNetwork:
  pods:
    cidrBlocks:
      - "10.244.0.0/16"
      - "fd42:77:2::/56"
  services:
    cidrBlocks:
      - "10.96.0.0/16"
      - "fd42:77:3::/112"

apiProxy:
  # Required: the CAPN identity Secret in the release namespace; its LXD
  # credentials let the hook find the load balancer and add the proxy device.
  infrastructureSecretName: ""
  # Host address the API listens on; "0.0.0.0" is every IPv4 address of the host.
  listenAddress: "0.0.0.0"
  # Host port; 0 = 20000 + (adler32 of cluster.name mod 10000).
  port: 0
  # Python 3 standard library only.
  image: "python:3.14.10-alpine3.24@sha256:5862d971d1f0ae26b258cefa4e893556b1d3aba81bd2ff30888704ad378bab67"
  # Deadline of each gate, in seconds. Their sum (45 min) stays below the
  # callers' Helm timeout of the release (50 min), so a failing gate reports
  # itself.
  timeoutSeconds:
    loadBalancer: 600
    kubeconfig: 1200
    proxy: 300
    livez: 600

# `helm test`: waits until the Cluster has converged (topology applied, nothing
# rolling out or scaling, Available).
tests:
  image: "registry.k8s.io/kubectl:v1.37.2@sha256:fe049faa65ae483ac200009a949a68fa4c9985daea12c9cb1195c9c7965301fc"
  # Deadline of each wait, in seconds; the caller's `helm test --timeout`
  # bounds the whole check.
  timeoutSeconds: 7200
```

## cni-calico

The Calico tigera-operator. It creates the Calico and operator.tigera.io CRDs
itself (`manageCRDs`, the upstream default); the Installation, the APIServer
and Gate B are in charts/cni-calico-config, installed after this release.

Version `2.0.0`, appVersion `v3.33.1`. Dependency `tigera-operator` `v3.33.1` from https://docs.tigera.io/calico/charts. No schema: the values pass through to the upstream chart.

```yaml
# The operator release renders no custom resources: they need the CRDs the
# operator creates at start-up. charts/cni-calico-config carries them.
tigera-operator:
  installation:
    enabled: false
  apiServer:
    enabled: false
  goldmane:
    enabled: false
  whisker:
    enabled: false
  # The upstream default tolerates every NoSchedule taint, the one a cordon adds
  # included: a drained operator Pod comes back on the node being drained, and
  # Cluster API's drain never ends. These are the NoSchedule taints it must run
  # on before the CNI is up (calico-typha's list); NoExecute stays as upstream.
  tolerations:
    - effect: NoExecute
      operator: Exists
    - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane
      effect: NoSchedule
      operator: Exists
    - key: node.kubernetes.io/not-ready
      effect: NoSchedule
      operator: Exists
    - key: node.kubernetes.io/network-unavailable
      effect: NoSchedule
      operator: Exists
    - key: node.cloudprovider.kubernetes.io/uninitialized
      effect: NoSchedule
      operator: Exists
    - key: CriticalAddonsOnly
      operator: Exists
```

## cni-calico-config

Calico configuration: the dual-stack Installation and the APIServer, and Gate B
as `helm test` (every node Ready; pods on two workers reachable over IPv4 and
IPv6). Installed after charts/cni-calico, whose operator creates the CRDs.

Version `2.0.0`, appVersion `v3.33.1`. `values.schema.json` validates the values (`additionalProperties: false`).

```yaml
# Pod CIDRs as [IPv4, IPv6]; they must be the Cluster's pod network.
calico:
  pods:
    cidrBlocks:
      - "10.244.0.0/16"
      - "fd42:77:2::/56"

# Gate B (`helm test`).
tests:
  # The servers and the client (Kubernetes' e2e test image: netexec, sh, dig, curl).
  image: "registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.66.1@sha256:6e2eef87d0dc77e070a7549bc5fdfa290c0fefe3359eb33c2ad1eda692fe66a4"
  # Waits until every node is Ready.
  kubectlImage: "registry.k8s.io/kubectl:v1.37.2@sha256:fe049faa65ae483ac200009a949a68fa4c9985daea12c9cb1195c9c7965301fc"
  # The port the client fetches; the servers listen on 8080, so another value
  # makes the gate fail (a negative test).
  probePort: 8080
  # For the nodes, then again for the endpoints.
  timeoutSeconds: 600
```

## metallb

Upstream MetalLB in native L2 mode (no FRR, no frr-k8s). The address pool, the
L2 advertisement and Gate A are in charts/metallb-config, installed after this
release: the upstream chart ships its CRDs as templates, so a pool in the same
release would not validate at install time.

Version `2.0.0`, appVersion `v0.16.2`. Dependency `metallb` `0.16.2` from https://metallb.github.io/metallb. No schema: the values pass through to the upstream chart.

```yaml
# Native mode: the speaker answers ARP/NDP itself; neither FRR nor frr-k8s (the
# upstream default since 0.15) runs. Everything else is upstream's default.
metallb:
  frrk8s:
    enabled: false
  speaker:
    frr:
      enabled: false
```

## metallb-config

The IPv6 address pool and its L2 advertisement (workers only, one interface),
and Gate A as `helm test` (a LoadBalancer Service gets a pool address and
answers). Installed after charts/metallb, which registers the CRDs.

Version `2.0.0`, appVersion `v0.16.2`. `values.schema.json` validates the values (`additionalProperties: false`).

```yaml
pool:
  # IPv6 addresses on the external network (required): "<first>-<last>". The
  # external network is IPv6 only; a range rather than a prefix keeps the
  # prefix's subnet-router address (`<prefix>::`) out of the pool.
  rangeV6: ""

l2:
  # Only workers announce, on eth1 (the network contract); `extraNodeSelectors`
  # narrows the workers further (matchLabels).
  extraNodeSelectors: {}

# Gate A (`helm test`).
tests:
  # Server and client (Kubernetes' e2e test image: netexec, sh, curl).
  image: "registry.k8s.io/e2e-test-images/agnhost:2.66.1@sha256:6e2eef87d0dc77e070a7549bc5fdfa290c0fefe3359eb33c2ad1eda692fe66a4"
  # The port the client fetches; the Service listens on 80, so another value
  # makes the gate fail (a negative test).
  probePort: 80
  timeoutSeconds: 300
```
